meta.actor: Claude — consolidation pass (no research, no content rewriting)
meta.scope: Every Grok batch file for Afghanistan merged into one file. Records are byte-faithful to the batches except for the normalisations listed in _consolidation.

reports.title: National Statistics and Information Authority (NSIA) institutional core
reports.publisher: National Statistics and Information Authority
reports.description: Primary national statistical office under the de facto authorities, responsible for censuses, surveys, national accounts, prices, demographic and multi-domain socio-economic statistics where published.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node. Data continuity, coverage and independence are severely constrained.

reports.title: Population census and estimates
reports.publisher: NSIA / UN-aligned
reports.description: Population estimates. Population is approximately 43–45 million; the age structure is very young and rapid population growth continues to pressure per-capita outcomes.
reports._url_evidence: UNFPA World Population Dashboard country page for Afghanistan; fetched page shows total population 43,800,000 (2025) and the 0-14 / 15-64 / 65+ age structure, matching the item's 43-45 million young-age-structure description. NSIA's own site is unreachable via WebFetch.

reports.title: National Accounts of Afghanistan (GDP)
reports.publisher: NSIA / related
reports.description: Official and compiled national accounts (GDP). The economy contracted sharply after 2021; recent fiscal years show modest real growth but per-capita outcomes remain under pressure from population growth and structural constraints.
reports._notes: Primary macroeconomic output node under constrained conditions.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics
reports.publisher: NSIA / Da Afghanistan Bank related
reports.description: CPI and inflation rates. Price dynamics have moderated relative to the immediate post-2021 shock but remain sensitive to exchange-rate, import and supply conditions.
reports._url_evidence: Da Afghanistan Bank's Monthly Inflation Report series page, fetched and confirmed to list 19 named monthly inflation reports (Jan 2020 - Jul 2021); note the series stopped in July 2021 and NSIA's CPI bulletin site is unreachable via WebFetch.

reports.title: Da Afghanistan Bank institutional and reporting core
reports.publisher: Da Afghanistan Bank
reports.description: Central bank responsible for monetary policy, foreign-exchange management and key macro-financial statistics. Publishes exchange rates, inflation references and limited monetary series.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and external accounts
reports.publisher: Da Afghanistan Bank / related
reports.description: BOP and external-sector statistics where available. Remittances, limited formal trade, humanitarian inflows and large informal/unrecorded flows are structural features under current conditions.
reports._notes: External-accounts node under constrained formal data and large informal flows.
reports._url_evidence: Da Afghanistan Bank External Sector Statistics page, fetched and confirmed to host 'Balance of Payments Transactions (BPM6)' and 'Net International Investment Position' files for Afghanistan; data stops at 2021.

reports.title: Afghanistan foundational statistical-system meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from NSIA and DAB sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding the NSIA institutional core, population, national accounts, CPI, Da Afghanistan Bank institutional role and BOP into the opening foundation layer for Afghan research.
reports._notes: Opening integrating node. Data quality, coverage and institutional constraints should be carried forward in all subsequent batches.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch

reports.title: Agriculture production statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock / NSIA related
reports.description: Statistics on crop and livestock production. Agriculture is the backbone of rural livelihoods and food security; wheat is the dominant staple. Production is highly sensitive to drought, water availability and input constraints.
reports._notes: Core primary-sector production node under constrained conditions.

reports.title: Wheat production and food-gap statistics
reports.publisher: MAIL / related
reports.description: Focused statistics on wheat production and the structural wheat gap. Domestic production typically falls short of national demand (around 4.5–5 million tonnes vs demand near 7 million tonnes), making imports and humanitarian food assistance critical.
reports._notes: Foundational food-security crop node. Structural production deficit is a defining feature.
reports._url_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for Afghanistan (12 Jan 2026), fetched and confirmed to state 2025 wheat production of 4.5 million tonnes and cereal import requirements of 3.7 million tonnes, matching the item's wheat-gap framing.

reports.title: Humanitarian needs and acute food insecurity statistics
reports.publisher: OCHA / Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan / IPC-aligned
reports.description: Statistics on people in need of humanitarian assistance and acute food insecurity. In 2026 an estimated 21.9 million people (roughly 45% of the population) require humanitarian assistance; acute food insecurity affects over 17 million, with several million in Emergency (IPC Phase 4).
reports._notes: Highest-centrality social and humanitarian node under current conditions.
reports._url_evidence: OCHA Afghanistan country page, fetched and confirmed to give the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan figures: 21.9 million people in need (~45% of population) and 17.5 million targeted; humanitarianaction.info blocks WebFetch with 403.

reports.title: Remittance inflows framing
reports.publisher: Derived from World Bank and related sources
reports.description: Framing of remittance inflows as a critical external financing and household-income source. Remittances support consumption and foreign-exchange availability under constrained formal capital flows.

reports.title: Afghanistan agriculture–humanitarian–remittances densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from MAIL, OCHA and external sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding agriculture and wheat statistics, humanitarian needs / acute food insecurity, and remittance inflows into a coherent primary-sector, humanitarian and external-financing layer under highly constrained conditions.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
National accounts, CPI, BOP and DAB series from Batch 1

reports.title: Exchange-rate and afghani statistics
reports.publisher: Da Afghanistan Bank
reports.description: Official exchange rates for the afghani against major currencies published by Da Afghanistan Bank. The rate is a central price signal for imports, remittances and domestic prices under limited formal capital flows.

reports.title: Women’s economic exclusion and labour-force framing
reports.publisher: Derived from UN Women and labour monitoring sources
reports.description: Framing of the severe restrictions on women’s participation in education, employment and public life. Women’s labour-force participation is extremely low (single-digit employment rates in recent estimates); the exclusion is projected to impose multi-year cumulative GDP losses and is the single most consequential constraint on recovery.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality structural and human-capital constraint node under current conditions.

reports.title: Border mobility and returnee statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from IOM and related monitoring sources
reports.description: Statistics on cross-border inflows and outflows, especially with Iran and Pakistan. Large-scale returns and ongoing mobility place pressure on host communities, services and livelihoods; formal trade and informal flows interact with these movements.
reports._url_evidence: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix Afghanistan page, fetched and confirmed to publish Flow Monitoring Snapshots on mobility at Afghanistan's border points with Iran and Pakistan, plus returnee and baseline area assessment datasets.

reports.title: Afghanistan exchange–women–border densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from DAB, UN Women and mobility sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding exchange-rate statistics, women’s economic exclusion framing, and border mobility/returnee statistics into a coherent monetary–human-capital–mobility layer under highly constrained conditions.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Remittances, humanitarian, agriculture and DAB series from earlier batches

reports.title: Education enrolment and girls’ secondary exclusion statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from UNICEF and education monitoring sources
reports.description: Statistics and framing of education access. Afghanistan remains the only country where secondary and higher education are effectively closed to girls and women; more than 2.6 million girls have been denied secondary education since 2021. The ban is a major human-capital and long-term growth constraint.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality education node under current restrictions. Directly linked to the women’s exclusion node.
reports._url_evidence: UNICEF Afghanistan education programme page, fetched and confirmed to report enrolment statistics (3.7 million children out of school, 60% of them girls) and education-restriction impacts.

reports.title: Life expectancy and health outcome statistics
reports.publisher: WHO / related
reports.description: Life expectancy at birth and related health indicators. Life expectancy remains among the lowest in the region; gains earlier in the century have been partially reversed. Continuously referenced in humanitarian and human-development analysis.
reports._notes: Core health-outcome densification under constrained service delivery.
reports._url_evidence: WHO country data page for Afghanistan, fetched and confirmed to publish 'Life expectancy at birth' and healthy life expectancy (HALE) by sex for Afghanistan, plus mortality and health-workforce indicators.

reports.title: Merchandise trade statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from World Bank and trade monitoring sources
reports.description: Statistics on merchandise exports and imports. Exports are small and concentrated in food products and textiles; India, Iran, Uzbekistan and China are notable destinations. Imports of essential goods dominate; the trade deficit is structural.
reports._notes: Core formal trade densification under constrained conditions.
reports._url_evidence: World Bank Afghanistan Development Update (May 2026), fetched and confirmed to report merchandise exports at 10.0% of GDP, merchandise imports at 65% of GDP (US$13.2bn in FY2025) and trade-corridor dependence on Pakistan, Iran and India.

reports.title: Afghanistan education–health–trade densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from education, health and trade sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding education enrolment and girls’ secondary exclusion, life expectancy/health outcomes, and merchandise trade statistics into a coherent human-capital and external layer under highly constrained conditions.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Women’s exclusion, humanitarian, remittances and BOP series from earlier batches

reports.title: Drought and water-stress statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from climate monitoring and humanitarian sources
reports.description: Statistics and monitoring on drought conditions, snowpack, soil moisture and water availability. Recurrent drought is a primary driver of food insecurity and rural livelihood stress; western and southern provinces are frequently the most affected.
reports._notes: High-centrality environmental constraint node linking agriculture and humanitarian needs.
reports._url_evidence: FEWS NET Afghanistan country page, fetched and confirmed to publish Food Security Outlooks and agroclimatology/Seasonal Monitor reporting on drought, rainfall, soil moisture and multi-year drought recovery.

reports.title: Kabul province economic and demographic framing
reports.publisher: Derived from spatial and statistical sources
reports.description: Framing of Kabul province as the dominant urban, administrative and services centre. Concentrates a large share of the national urban population and economic activity relative to other provinces.

reports.title: Herat province economic and trade framing
reports.publisher: Derived from spatial and trade sources
reports.description: Framing of Herat as the principal western commercial and trade hub, with strong links to Iran and a large urban population. Frequently ranks among the more economically active provinces outside Kabul.

reports.title: Balkh province economic and trade framing
reports.publisher: Derived from spatial and trade sources
reports.description: Framing of Balkh (including Mazar-i-Sharif) as the principal northern commercial and trade hub, with links to Uzbekistan and Central Asia. An important secondary urban and economic pole.

reports.title: Afghanistan climate–provincial densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from climate and spatial sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding drought/water-stress statistics and the Kabul, Herat and Balkh provincial framings into a coherent environmental and spatial layer under highly constrained conditions.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Agriculture, humanitarian, trade and population series from earlier batches

_consolidation.json_syntax_repair_note: These batch files were not valid JSON as delivered: "releases_per_year" carried an unquoted text value (missing opening quote), e.g. `"releases_per_year": continuous",`. Repaired mechanically by re-quoting the value verbatim. No number was invented.
_consolidation.cadence_note: A non-numeric cadence text was moved off releases_per_year into _cadence_original verbatim and the numeric field omitted, per the v2 spec (omitted, never null). Needs a human/judgement pass to become a real number.
_consolidation.filename_note: Filed as afg- not af-: `af-` is already the Africa prefix in this repo (see grok-import-progress.md). Report ids inside this file still start `af-` as Grok wrote them and will need re-prefixing to `afg-` before they can be minted alongside the Africa branch.

_normalisation.note: Second pass, 2026-08-18: mechanical alignment to src/lib/types.ts. Nothing researched, nothing invented. Every original value that was replaced is preserved on the record under a key prefixed with an underscore.
rules: jurisdiction_level mapped into the six-value union; the delivered string kept as _jurisdiction_level_original.
domains: format-normalised, then any tag outside the 22 approved values prefixed "proposed:" as the spec directs. No semantic merging was done — that needs your call.

relationship_type: part_of edges moved onto the child node as part_of; contains edges reversed onto the child; produced_by edges dropped (publisher is a string, not a node); related_to / complements held in _dropped as deferred. Off-union values were poisoning every PageRank score with NaN.
last_updated added as null where absent (required field, string|null).
region filled with the country name where it was null or missing.
releases_per_year: unambiguous single-word cadences resolved to numbers; ambiguous text left in _cadence_original and listed under _gaps.unresolved_cadence.
source_kind mapped to official/commercial; delivered value kept as _source_kind_original.
Non-schema keys Grok wrote (shape, notes, referenced_by, ...) renamed with a leading underscore so they are visibly not part of the schema. Nothing deleted.

_gaps.note: What is genuinely missing and cannot be fixed mechanically — this is the research queue, not a defect list.

url_research_pass.method: Per-country web research. A URL was accepted only when the page was actually retrieved and its content confirmed the publication. Publisher homepages, Wikipedia, news, aggregators and mirrors were rejected. Confirmations are stored on each node as _url_evidence.

_gaps.not_a_publication_note: These 11 nodes were checked against the web and are not published documents — synthesised 'meta'/'framing' nodes that only bind other nodes together, geographic areas, industries, projects, or institutions. The data spec (2b/2c) bans all of these. They are flagged in place with _flagged_not_a_publication rather than deleted, so you can strip them in one pass once you agree. 0 dependency edges in this file touch one.
